movement_source: row 'Common Equity Tier 1 (APRA Level 2)', column 30 Jun 20 column -> column 30 Jun 21 column
headline: CBA's APRA Level 2 CET1 ratio rose 150 bps to 13.1% in FY21 (from 11.6% in FY20), driven by strong organic capital generation from earnings (+185 bps across both halves), divestment proceeds (+42 bps), and an APRA operational risk add-on reduction (+17 bps), partially offset by dividends paid (-91 bps) and a modest net RWA increase (-5 bps). The internationally comparable CET1 ratio was 19.4% (up 200 bps from 17.4%).

drivers.columns: Jun 20 vs Jun 20 | Jun 21 vs Dec 20
drivers.narrative: Capital generated from earnings contributed +88 bps in 2H20 and +97 bps in 1H21 (excluding net equity accounted profits from associates), totaling +185 bps for the full year. The bank states business fundamentals remained strong with cash NPAT supporting CET1 throughout FY21.

drivers.columns: Jun 20 vs Dec 20 | Dec 20 vs Jun 21
drivers.narrative: Total dividends reduced CET1 by -91 bps: the 2020 final dividend (DRP satisfied by issuance of $264 million shares) contributed -32 bps, and the 2021 interim dividend (DRP neutralised by on-market purchase of $418 million shares) contributed -59 bps.

Divestment proceeds contributed +42 bps, including the receipt of final proceeds from the sale of CommInsure Life (+2 bps) and the completion of the sale of PT Commonwealth Life. Additional proceeds from Colonial First State and CommInsure General Insurance were expected but not yet completed.
APRA's November 2020 announcement resulted in a 50% reduction in CBA's operational RWA add-on (from $12.5 billion to $6.25 billion), contributing +17 bps to the CET1 ratio in 2H20.

drivers.columns: Jun 20 vs Dec 20 | Dec 20 vs Jun 21
drivers.narrative: Net RWA movement was -5 bps: underlying RWA decreased by -13 bps in 2H20 (driven by reductions in Operational Risk RWA, Traded Market Risk RWA, and IRRBB RWA, partly offset by higher Credit Risk RWA), while RWA increased by +8 bps in 1H21.

drivers.columns: Jun 20 vs Dec 20 | Dec 20 vs Jun 21
drivers.narrative: Other movements contributed -2 bps in 2H20 and +4 bps in 1H21, netting +2 bps for the full year. The 1H21 'other' includes the CommInsure Life sale proceeds impact of +2 bps.

limitations: The walk chart on page 111 of the results presentation is the primary source for the full-year decomposition. The profit announcement (page 53) only discloses half-on-half drivers for 1H21, not the full-year breakdown.
The bank does not separately quantify the full-year earnings generation driver; the +185 bps figure is derived by summing the 2H20 (+88 bps) and 1H21 (+97 bps) Cash NPAT bars from the walk chart.
No off-market buy-back occurred in FY21; the $6 billion buy-back mentioned on page 13 was announced but not executed within the period.

Capped at 80: earnings_generation +185 bps, dividend_net_drp -91 bps, rwa -5 bps. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.

evidence_records.quote: The Bank's CET1 ratio (APRA) was 11.6% as at 30 June 2020
Reflects APRA's announcement on 20 November 2020 resulting in a 50% reduction in CBA's operational RWA add-on (from $12.5bn to $6.25bn).
2020 final dividend: included the issuance of shares in respect of the Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP).
2021 interim dividend included the on-market purchase of shares in respect of the DRP.
Includes the receipt of the final proceeds from the sale of CommInsure Life (+2bpts)

Key drivers of the change in CET1 for the 6 months ended 30 June 2021 were capital generated from earnings (+97 basis points, excluding net equity accounted profits from associates), lower total RWA (+8 basis points) and other regulatory adjustments (+4 basis points), partly offset by the 2021 interim dividend (-59 basis points) in which the DRP was satisfied in full by the on-market purchase of shares.
